text:
emma_support: FYI customer (AcmeHealth) reports p99 jump to ~4-6s and intermittent 502/401s hitting Dedicated pool eu-prod-dedicated-7 since 08:12 UTC. They say it started after a heavy billing-window burst. Stacktrace snippets attached.

mike_sre: looking. is this strictly Dedicated? any hosted fallbacks triggered?

emma_support: yes only Dedicated. Hosted API routes fine. Customer traffic is large batched embed + gen calls.

jordan_oncall: metrics show scale-up attempts at 08:11:59 -> lots of pending attach requests. queue_length spiked to 850, attach_success rate dropped. p95 climbed first then p99.

alexa_eng: seeing auth service (token-refresh) error 429s correlated at same time. Clients keep retrying and hammering attach path. sample log:

```
ERROR attach: failed to attach model=redwood-v1 pool=eu-prod-dedicated-7 err="auth: refresh 429" attempts=6
```

infra_lead: sounds like a mixed failure: dedicated pool saturation + auth throttling -> attach retries queueing -> cold-gpu starts back up slower than normal (warmup concurrency limited). We should do short-term mitigations and then a repro + postmortem.

emma_support: customer provided repro steps: 1) fire 200 concurrent requests with bursty timeline across 10s 2) use long context (2k tokens) 3) include Authorization header with short-lived token. They see 401 after a few minutes.

mike_sre: repro attempt in staging now. plan: (A) throttle token-refresh retries with jitter (B) raise minpool for that pool temporarily (C) enable extra prewarm slots (D) route high-priority customers to hosted fallback while we stabilize.

cloudinfra_bot: deploy status: autoscaler-config v3.14 -> rolled 2026-03-16 07:50 UTC

alexa_eng: quick commands to run if we need manual mitigation:
``` 
# raise minpool to avoid coldstarts
redwoodctl pools set-min eu-prod-dedicated-7 --min 6

# enable prewarm workers
redwoodctl prewarm enable --pool eu-prod-dedicated-7 --count 2

# tighten attach retry jitter
redwoodctl config set autoscaler.attach_retry_jitter_ms 250
```

jordan_oncall: also add token-refresh rate-limit on client-side (support guide) and temp bump auth service quota for Dedicated clients: /ops/auth/quota adjust --client acmehealth --burst 200

mike_sre: running repro script now (in background). Observing attach queue slow drain and repeated "worker cold-init" logs for a subset of GPUs. Looks like kernel image pull plus model cache init is ~15-18s under this load which cascades into p99.

emma_support: customer asked for ETA on fix. I told them we'll apply mitigations and follow up with root cause.

infra_lead: applying mitigations in this order: 1) prewarm enable 2) set-min 6 3) temporary routing rule for priority customers to hosted. Will monitor for 15m.

cloudinfra_bot: action_log: prewarm enable success, set-min success. routing rule created -> hosted-fallback=on for tag:priority-cust

alexa_eng: after mitigations p99 dropped from ~5.8s -> ~1.2s for the affected customers, attach-error 502/401 count down by ~90% in the first 8 minutes. Looks stable so far.

mike_sre: still seeing a small tail of 401s — auth team says token refresh refresh window overlapped with billing auth surge. We'll ask them to patch to exponential backoff and increase server-side concurrency limits.

emma_support: relayed to customer, they're ok with temporary routing. I'll open a ticket and schedule postmortem. Thanks all :thumbsup:

infra_lead: next steps for PMR: collect attach traces, kernel pull times, auth throttle traces, autoscaler event log. We'll propose: increase default minpool for heavy burst customers, better client-side rate-limit guidance, and introduce randomized jitter on attach retry by default.

jordan_oncall: putting a short runbook note in support playbook: "Dedicated burst mitigation" with commands we ran.

emma_support: creating postmortem ticket and adding timeline + mitigations. closing thread once I confirm customer's long-term fix.
